text:
support-ops: FYI - multiple customers reporting p99 spikes (~600-800ms) to the EU endpoints since ~12:25 UTC. Primarily TLS handshake / initial connect tails. Seen in our support traces and from synthetic probes. :rotating_light:

oncall-liz: Can you paste a repro curl or probe and one trace id we can look at?

support-ops: repro curl: `time curl -sv https://api.redwood-inference.eu/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -o /dev/null` -> connect 0.10s, TLS handshake 0.62s, total 0.74s. Trace id: trace=ri:eu:42a7fa32 (attached sample).

net-arnav: grabbing traceroute/tcpdump from the affected POP (eu-west-pop3). Short summary: at ~12:24 we saw routing changes - upstream path shifted through a different transit. Traceroute snippet below:

```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.eu (198.51.100.24), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.70.0.1  0.23 ms  0.21 ms  0.19 ms
 2  192.0.2.1  1.34 ms  1.29 ms  1.25 ms
 3  203.0.113.7  12.64 ms  12.60 ms  12.71 ms
 4  * * *
 5  198.51.100.1  110.12 ms  112.33 ms  109.98 ms
```

net-arnav: tcpdump shows repeated SYN retransmits on the path hop before our edge, and a 100ms extra RTT introduced at that hop. Looks like an upstream transit queued them or rerouted mid-flow.

sre-jen: Was anything changed around routing/GSLB? I saw a canary for the GSLB weight recalculation at 12:20-12:26 in deploy logs.

infra-dan: deploy-bot shows: `deploy-bot: canary deploy gslb-weight-v2 -> 12:20 UTC -> 12:27 UTC (20% traffic)`

net-arnav: that matches. My hypothesis: the new weight calc nudged a subset of traffic to a different upstream peer with a longer egress queue/tail. That explains the TLS handshake tail (handshake includes multiple RTTs) and p99 blowups.

oncall-liz: Immediate mitigation options?

net-arnav: short term: pin affected POP to previous GSLB weights (force 100% to previous path) or increase retries/timeouts on the edge so SYN retransmits don't add that many ms. But a rollback of the canary will be fastest to measure.

infra-dan: I can roll back the canary now. Reverting gslb-weight-v2 -> scaling weight back to gslb-weight-v1 for eu-west-pop3. Triggering rollback...

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback gslb-weight-v2 -> SUCCESS (12:37 UTC)

support-ops: after rollback, some customers reporting improved p99 to ~120-180ms. We're seeing reduced SYN retransmits in tcpdump.

sre-jen: Good. Please keep monitoring for 30m. We'll capture full packet captures and BGP update logs for the window 12:15-12:45 for postmortem.

product-amy: Customer impact notes: at least three paid customers flagged this as a production regression. We should include severity and notify CSMs.

net-arnav: action items: 1) Collect BGP/peering changes + transit provider logs during 12:15-12:45. 2) Run controlled probe replays to confirm which upstream adds ~100ms. 3) Add a GSLB safety check to avoid moving >10% traffic to a path with >50ms added median RTT.

infra-dan: also adding a canary rollback playbook step for the next deploy (auto-rollback if p99 increases by >2x in 5m).

sre-jen: filing incident ticket and assigning owners for postmortem. Short-term status: mitigated by rollback, currently monitoring.

support-ops: I'll update customers and CSMs and include the trace id list.

product-amy: thanks everyone. Let's capture the postmortem once we have the BGP/traceroute artifacts. :white_check_mark:
